definitions: Marketing page

One agreed URL with a defined audience, purpose and approved outline, using an agreed page type. Home, individual service, about, contact and proof pages count. Write as much or as little as the topic, reader and search intent require. No fixed word cap and no extra charge solely because approved content needs more words. New audiences, topics, research methods, templates or functions are scope changes agreed before work.
Researched practical guide

One buyer question answered through an approved outline, client expertise and bounded desk research, with sources checked and linked. Depth is set by the question rather than word count. It differs from a standard service page by its research and explanatory purpose. Included Business/Signature guides use page slots. A guide in Local Search Partnership consumes its two monthly content/SEO units. No ranking guarantee.
Policy page
Up to three client-approved policy texts can be formatted outside a website plan's marketing-page cap. W&M is not being hired to draft legal policies or determine their adequacy.
Content collection entry

A supplied record placed into an agreed reusable template, such as a project or team member. Collection-entry limits are separate from marketing pages because original writing and unique design are not included for each entry. A separately written entry uses a marketing-page allocation or module.
Simple website graphic
A single supporting diagram, icon arrangement or illustration for an agreed page. Full identity design, complex infographics, 3D and open-ended illustration are separately scoped.
Existing-tool link/embed
Place and style an already-configured supported tool. Creating its service rules, calendars, payment logic, CRM fields or automations is setup work and uses the relevant module/sprint.
Revision round

One compiled feedback list from one approver for the current stage, followed by one implementation pass. Refinement within the agreed direction is included; a different concept, new audience or added functionality is a change request. Correcting a defect is not a paid revision round.
Acceptance
Completion of the named deliverables and written tests, followed by explicit client approval. Silence is not treated as launch permission.
Defect

A delivered item failing the agreed acceptance criteria because of W&M's implementation. Correct it without using a client's monthly output allowance. New preferences, new requirements and subsequent third-party changes are different work.
Complete project hours

Include discovery, research, copy, design, production, QA, calls, messages, revisions, handoff and expected defect correction. Internal hours help price scope; they are not a hidden limit that lets W&M abandon an agreed fixed deliverable.
Writing scope without word caps

Agree the page purpose, topic/question, available evidence, research method, deliverables and review rounds before booking. The agreed research is client facts plus ordinary desk/query research; original interviews, surveys, specialist legal/scientific research or additional topics require a separate scope. W&M absorbs its own underestimation. Extra length required for the unchanged approved purpose does not trigger a fee.
delivery: Readiness and queue

Allow roughly one week for collecting inputs as an initial planning allowance, but do not promise that client-controlled readiness has a fixed duration. State the next available start separately from the plan's active delivery range.
Owner work and elapsed time

The quoted calendar is not a billable-hour claim. Short builds can finish earlier by explicit agreement after every gate passes. Do not promise same-day or four-hour delivery from the owner’s internal estimate. Readiness and the sales queue remain separate from the booked delivery window.
Working calendar

Project weeks are calendar weeks, with work scheduled Monday–Friday, 9am–5pm America/New_York, excluding announced holidays. Project day ranges are business days. Days in a monthly cycle are calendar days of that billing cycle; schedule actual work/reviews on business days.
Feedback

Plan for consolidated feedback within two business days at each gate. Normal review time is included in the planned range; the shortest endpoint requires the prompt approvals stated in that plan. Agree longer review windows before booking.
Weekly update
For active projects, send one weekly update with completed work, preview/evidence, decisions needed, blockers and the next dated milestone. This is included delivery work.
Calls are optional

Written intake, approvals, review and support are the default for every plan/module. All W&M interviews, workshops, sessions, training and walkthroughs elsewhere mean written exchanges plus recorded demonstrations, with the stated appointment available by choice. The appointment substitutes for the corresponding exchange; it does not stack unlimited additional consulting. Provide the same decisions, instructions and acceptance evidence either way. Vendor identity/video verification can still be required by the vendor.
Questions and incidents

Send email or messages through the agreed text channel at any time, including nights/weekends. During active projects, paid monthly service and applicable clarification/defect windows, acknowledge within one business day, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm America/New_York excluding announced holidays. Give the next action and a separate resolution estimate. Care site-down/failed-checkout reports receive triage within one business day. Messages are not continuously monitored; 24/7 submission is not 24/7 staffing, instant response or unlimited new work.
Client delay

Notify the owner when a missing decision threatens a milestone. After five business days beyond the agreed response deadline, issue a pause notice and release the production slot. Resume at the next mutually agreed slot with a new date; do not silently continue charging project labor for waiting.
Change requests

State the requested change, exact deliverable, additional fee and schedule effect. Obtain written agreement before doing it. An internal under-estimate of unchanged agreed scope is W&M's responsibility.
W&M delay

Notify promptly, keep the agreed scope, provide a dated recovery plan and offer the appropriate reschedule/credit/refund for work not delivered. Do not blame the client for an unrecorded internal capacity problem.
Launch control
Launch only after explicit approval and the named acceptance checks. Preserve the agreed rollback path and avoid moving DNS, email or live payments without the owner-approved cutover plan.
Post-launch

For website/store builds, check within two business days and around day 14. Defect-reporting windows: Focused/Store 30 days; Custom/Business 60; Signature 90. Timely reported defects remain covered until corrected. Business/Signature include one bounded day-30 review of launch observations, no new campaign.
No silent service substitution
If an included tool or platform capability proves unavailable, explain the limitation and agree an equivalent deliverable or revised scope/fee before treating the project as complete.
Monthly cycle completion

All monthly deliverables must finish within the paid billing cycle, including February and other short cycles. Schedule review, QA and reporting on business days by cycle end; a numbered stage never extends the paid cycle automatically.
Daily communication allocation

Reserve acknowledgement and follow-up time each business day inside the delivery/admin budgets. Record actual message, recording and optional appointment time; reforecast returning revisions and support as soon as the reserved allowance is threatened. Keep the accepted deliverable and response standard.
payments: Website and store payments

40% to reserve the agreed start, 30% after approval of copy/design direction, and 30% after staging acceptance before the scheduled launch. Show dollar amounts and milestone definitions in the proposal. No production work starts without agreed scope and initial payment.
Finite sprints and discovery
50% at booking and 50% on delivery/acceptance of the agreed output. Local Presence Setup's final milestone is completion of the specified work and handoff, not a platform verification outcome.
Modules

Standalone modules use 50/50 payment; modules added to a build use that build's written milestones. Care onboarding is paid before onboarding starts and must pass eligibility before recurring service begins.
Monthly service

Bill one month in advance on an agreed date. Month-to-month, no annual lock-in. Cancellation received before the next billing date prevents the next renewal; the current paid cycle remains available. Show renewal and cancellation instructions before enrollment.
Unused monthly work

Client-unused edit/output allocations do not accumulate indefinitely. By day 10, flag missing inputs and propose a pre-approved alternative. If no useful work can proceed, agree a pause before the next cycle. If W&M misses an agreed output for its own reasons, the client chooses a dated carry-forward or a proportionate credit/refund for the undelivered portion; do not sell the same output again.
Project cancellation

Use a written reconciliation: pay for completed agreed work and approved nonrecoverable external expenses; return unearned prepaid fees. Define the reconciliation and payment timetable in the proposal instead of calling every deposit nonrefundable. Existing client agreements keep their terms.
Outside costs

List domain, hosting/platform, stock/fonts, apps, payment/integration usage, backup tools and other third-party fees before signing. Prices here are W&M service fees in USD; show any applicable tax separately. No subcontractor or unusual license is assumed free.
Reuse and credits

Roadmap reuse: a later proposal itemizes the diagnosis actually reused and a corresponding credit, limited to work removed and the prior paid fee. No automatic full-credit promise or arbitrary expiry. Unchanged implementation work stays priced.
Accounts

The client owns the domain and business/platform accounts from the beginning where the provider supports it; W&M uses delegated access. Client-owned pre-existing accounts and data are never withheld as a substitute for collecting a disputed invoice.
Deliverables and licenses

Transfer agreed original deliverables and editable source files under the project agreement after the relevant fees are paid. Identify licensed fonts, stock media, open-source components, third-party platform restrictions and AI-assisted assets separately. Do not promise exclusive ownership of licensed or generated material.
Exit

Provide the current account/license/export inventory and agreed source files. Remove delegated access when requested after handoff; explain any platform export limits. A new migration or training beyond the agreed handoff is quoted before work. For Google Business Profile, follow the platform's prompt separation rules.
Replacement modules

When a module replaces included work, quote only the incremental work. For example, a guided form replacing an included ordinary form removes that ordinary form production/testing line from the build estimate before the upgrade fee is agreed. Retain the acceptance tests that still apply.
Module review and defect support

Standalone modules include one consolidated review round unless their scope explicitly includes two. Production/design/setup modules receive handoff and a 30-day defect-reporting window for W&M-delivered work. M9 has its stated 30-day platform follow-up checks, with no guaranteed platform decision; M12 support is named in its quote. Assessment/strategy-only deliverables receive 14 days of clarification and factual correction.
launchChecks: Where these checks apply

Apply the relevant shared checks to every website/store build and to the pages, configurations and journeys changed by Repair, Workflow, monthly production and standalone modules. A module does not include an unrelated whole-site audit. Tests must still cover any shared component it changes.
Content and scope

Reconcile the signed page/form/collection inventory. Check approved business facts, titles, descriptions, headings, links, image alt text and permissioned assets. Verify the client-approved policy texts are present.
Layouts and accessibility checks

Check agreed mobile/desktop widths, keyboard navigation, visible focus, headings, labels, contrast, validation and reduced-motion behavior. Use automated checks plus manual review of essential journeys. Use WCAG 2.2 AA as the design/testing reference; do not call this an independent certification or exhaustive conformance audit.
Browser and journey checks

Test current Chrome and Firefox plus WebKit-based coverage for essential journeys. Record actual versions and any real-device checks; do not label an emulation result as a physical-device test. Verify form receipt and confirmation; for stores, verify the agreed transaction scenarios.
Performance

Agree representative routes and budgets at kickoff. For W&M-controlled pages, propose three desktop and three mobile lab runs per representative page: median FCP ≤1.8s, LCP ≤2.5s, TBT ≤200ms and Speed Index ≤3.4s; worst CLS ≤0.1. Include the homepage and each materially different key page/journey type. Save reports and remedy W&M-controlled failures before launch. Record and pin the runner/browser version, viewport, network/CPU throttling, cache state and test environment; use the same settings for comparison.
Performance limits

Third-party checkout, hosted-platform constraints and vendor scripts must be identified before booking. Any necessary exception needs a specific documented cause, effect and client acceptance; do not silently lower budgets to obtain a pass. Lab runs do not guarantee every real visitor's result or replace field Core Web Vitals, which include INP.
Search foundations

Check indexability/canonicals, sitemap, metadata, relevant structured data and agreed redirects. Verify or submit to Search Console if access is available. These are launch tasks, not a promise of indexing, ranking or traffic.
Measurement

All four website plans include one native GA4/Search Console setup and one inquiry-success event, with compatible consent configuration from client-approved settings. M1 removes that work when quoting an upgrade. No personal form data in events.
Ownership and handoff

Deliver account/license inventory, agreed source files, written editing guide with recorded demonstration, recovery responsibilities, tested contact/booking path, outside-cost list and support dates. Verify account access and demonstrate at least one real editing task in the recording; obtain written confirmation that the owner can access the agreed editing workflow. Optional live training is available within the plan allocation.
Completion record

Save scope inventory, approval dates, test versions/results, known accepted limitations, launch/cutover record and support end date. This is evidence of the delivered work rather than a marketing badge.
